transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As we prepare for the Northlake University exclusive license signing next Monday, I need to run through our standard pre-signing review. The current draft grants worldwide exclusivity at a 3% running royalty, and the business team wants access to the technology immediately after execution. Before I finalize the approval package, I need each of your areas to flag anything that should change the deal. Let's start with IP — are there any concerns with the scope of the patent applications or the exclusivity grant? And licensing finance, do the royalty terms and financial commitments look workable? Patent prosecution, any issues with the pending applications we should address before signing? And export-controls counsel, does worldwide exclusivity raise any red flags given the medical-device platform? I want to surface every issue now so we're not scrambling over the weekend.

transcript.text: Thank you all for these thorough flags. Let me summarize where we stand and what I'm going to recommend to the business team. Third, Sofia's royalty benchmark showing the 3% rate is 75 basis points above the validated 225-basis-point market ceiling — we should renegotiate down to that ceiling. Given the cumulative weight of these issues, I do not believe we should sign on Monday as scheduled. My recommendation to the business team will be to seek a short extension from Northlake — even a week — to allow us to incorporate the carveout, resolve the chain-of-title issue, add the export-controls provisions, and renegotiate the royalty. Does anyone disagree with this approach, or have I accurately captured your concerns?
